title: Ontological Validation of Biomedical Topic Models: SNOMED CT Hierarchy Distance as an Automated Evaluation Metric
task: Post hoc clinical-plausibility diagnostic for biomedical topic models
problem: Word co-occurrence coherence (UMass, Cv) encodes no clinical knowledge and cannot flag topics that merge clinically unrelated entities.
architecture: Curated clinical concepts (about 50-75 per specialty) mapped to SNOMED CT; per-topic mean Wu-Palmer distance (via lowest common ancestor) between concepts in the same topic, compared with a cross-topic baseline using Cohen's d and Mann-Whitney tests; two-stage UMLS-CUI stopword filter (frequency, then semantic type).
llm_or_encoder: BERTopic arms with mxbai, PubMedBERT, BioLORD, SapBERT, ensemble, cui2vec, Snomed2Vec and other embeddings

datasets.name: Vascular surgery corpus
datasets.details: 47,318 articles from 8 journals; single-journal JVS subset 14,290 articles

key_results: Craniofacial: BERTopic within-topic distance 0.343 vs cross-topic 0.768 (Cohen's d +0.159); LDA, NMF and Top2Vec give negative d (-0.043, -0.046, -0.050).
Vascular: recommended PubMedBERT+BioLORD ensemble gives 37 topics, Cv 0.792, 18.3% outliers.
Embedding cosine vs SNOMED similarity: |rho| < 0.08 across 10 model-corpus combinations.
Flags clinically mixed topics such as AAA repair with deep vein thrombosis (d = 0.600).
strengths: Adds domain-ontology validity to topic evaluation, which coherence misses.
Automated after one-time concept curation; tested on two corpora, eight embeddings and four model families.

limitations.text: Threshold d > 0.5 is heuristic and specialty-sensitive; topics with fewer than two mapped concepts cannot be scored.
Keyword mapping covers 78.8% (vascular) and 61.0% (craniofacial) of articles; only surgical specialties tested.
Clinician check was one joint discussion by three surgeons without blinding or rubric, so it cannot establish validity.

notes: Also reports that HDBSCAN min_cluster_size affected clinical validity more than embedding choice.
